message.content: The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large—on the order of 10^43. In other words, there are roughly ten‑trillion‑trillion‑trillion‑trillion‑trillion‑trillion different ways the pieces can be arranged on the board while still respecting the rules of the game.
